ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the bottom end of an inclined plane with an angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$ is connected to the left end of a conveyor belt at point B. The conveyor belt rotates clockwise at a speed of $v_{0}=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. A small coal block (which can be treated as a point mass) is released from the top of the inclined plane with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and slides down the incline. When the block reaches the bottom of the incline, its velocity becomes zero, and it is then carried by the conveyor belt to point C. The length of the inclined plane AB is $L_{1}{=}6\mathrm{m}$, the length of the conveyor belt BC is $L_{2}{=}4\mathrm{m}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the conveyor belt is $\mu_{2}{=}0.4$ ($\sin37^{\circ}{=}0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}{=}0.8$, $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$).

1. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the coal block and the inclined plane is $\mu_{1}$.
2. The time the coal block moves on the conveyor belt and the length of the scratch left on the conveyor belt.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the high place on the left is marked A, and the coal block is located on the inclined plane near A; the inclined plane slopes from the upper left toward the lower right and connects to point B, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is marked θ. Point B is the left end of the horizontal conveyor belt, and the right end is marked C. Beside the upper surface of the conveyor belt there is an arrow pointing to the right, indicating that the upper surface moves from B toward C. Reasoning: 1. On the inclined plane, take the downward direction along AB as the positive direction. When the coal block enters the inclined plane, its velocity is v_A=4 m/s; at point B, its velocity is v_B=0, and the displacement is L_1=6 m. From the kinematic formula v_B^2-v_A^2=2aL_1, obtain 0^2-4^2=2a\times 6, a=-\frac{16}{12}=-\frac{4}{3} m/s^2. The negative sign indicates that when the coal block moves downward along the inclined plane, it undergoes decelerated motion. The force equation in the inclined-plane direction is mg\sin\theta-\mu_1 mg\cos\theta=ma. Substitute sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, g=10: 10\times0.6-\mu_1\times10\times0.8=-\frac{4}{3}, 6-8\mu_1=-\frac{4}{3}, 8\mu_1=\frac{22}{3}, \mu_1=\frac{11}{12}. 2. When the coal block reaches point B, its velocity relative to the ground is 0, while the velocity of the upper surface of the conveyor belt to the right is v_0=4 m/s, so the coal block first slides relative to the conveyor belt and is subjected to kinetic friction to the right. Its acceleration is a_2=\mu_2 g=0.4\times10=4 m/s^2. The time required for the coal block to accelerate from 0 to 4 m/s is t_1=\frac{4}{4}=1 s. During this time, the displacement of the coal block is x_1=\frac12 a_2 t_1^2=\frac12\times4\times1^2=2 m. Since 2 m<BC=4 m, after the coal block reaches the conveyor-belt speed, it must still move uniformly with the conveyor belt for the remaining x_2=4-2=2 m. The uniform-motion time is t_2=\frac{x_2}{v_0}=\frac{2}{4}=0.5 s. Therefore the total motion time of the coal block on the conveyor belt is t=t_1+t_2=1+0.5=1.5 s. The scratch length is produced only during the relative sliding stage. During the sliding stage, the displacement of the conveyor belt is s_{belt}=v_0t_1=4\times1=4 m, the displacement of the coal block is x_1=2 m, and the relative displacement, namely the scratch length, is \Delta s=4-2=2 m.

s_{belt}=v_0t_1=4\times1=4 m,
the displacement of the coal block is x_1=2 m,
and the relative displacement, namely the scratch length, is
\Delta s=4-2=2 m.
